title: Activate safe native hyperlink interaction
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C5 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Consumes Orbit ORB-C6 and the exact accepted ORBF/ORBS proof revision current at activation.
- Preserves VEN-C1, VEN-C2, and VEN-C4. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

Orbit already emits explicit OSC 8 hyperlink URIs and Venus preserves each URI in its immutable scene, but Venus offers no native hyperlink action. Users therefore see linked text without a safe way to inspect, copy, or open the authoritative target.

## Evidence

- `src/scene.rs:42-48` stores the Orbit-authored hyperlink on each DrawCell.
- `src/scene.rs:285-297` materializes the URI directly from the canonical frame without reparsing terminal text.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:8-11` proves scene materialization and semantic input but indexes no hyperlink interaction.
- Orbit `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27` proves ORB-C6 and identifies rich presentation as an owned cross-repository boundary.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pointer hit testing against only the last successfully presented scene.
- Clear hover/focus affordance, target inspection, copy-link, and an explicit modifier-click or equivalent open action.
- A narrow scheme and length policy with bounded failure UX.
- Linux proof with a macOS-credible native-action seam.

Out of scope:
- Parsing URLs or file paths from ordinary terminal text.
- Silently opening a target, hiding the actual URI, or bypassing terminal mouse-reporting semantics.
- Workspace file navigation, custom schemes, shell integration, or any Orbit protocol/schema change unless a confirmed owner gap is reported back to Orbit.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, add the user-approved VEN-C5 row to docs/CONTRACTS.md and record the exact consumed Orbit proof and compatibility classification.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: the current OSC 8 specification or Ghostty VT documentation, the exact winit pointer/cursor APIs already selected, and official Linux/macOS external-open behavior. Compare only the native/standard-library path and credible opener crates if an opener dependency is actually needed.
3. Specify the interaction so terminal mouse reporting and selection retain priority; prefer an explicit modifier or context action rather than stealing ordinary clicks.
4. Derive link spans and hit targets from the accepted Scene. Do not add a second parser or mutable hyperlink model.
5. Apply URI size and scheme policy before invoking a native action. Opening and copying remain user-triggered.
6. Add one strong deterministic scene/hit/action-policy test and focused native dogfood.

Dependency decision: no crate is selected. A direct crate or architecture-shaping feature requires the Venus Crate gate and user approval before manifest edits.

Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency for external opening; scene identity, hit testing, and URI policy remain neutral.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if ORBF no longer carries one unambiguous target for the presented link.
- Stop if the design requires reparsing text, changing terminal authority, or adding a protocol adapter.
- Stop for user choice if safe platform opening requires a new dependency or materially different Linux/macOS policy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. VEN-C5 is approved and indexed before implementation, with the exact consumed ORB-C6 proof revision.
2. Hover, keyboard/context inspection, copy, and explicit open operate only on the last successfully presented scene and never on stale or unpresented geometry.
3. Links spanning multiple cells resolve to the exact Orbit-authored URI; resize, reconnect, revision replacement, wide cells, and renderer recovery cannot activate a stale target.
4. Ordinary clicks continue to follow terminal mouse and selection policy; opening is explicit and never silent.
5. Unsupported schemes, oversized or malformed targets, and native-open failure produce bounded, accessible UX.
6. Deterministic checks cover target identity, geometry invalidation, policy, and failure. Manual Linux dogfood covers hover, copy, open, terminal mouse mode, and keyboard access.
7. Canonical locked Rust checks and git diff --check pass, and every touched proved contract advances to an accepted proof commit or retains an explicit gap.
8. Closure records compatibility, dependency disposition, portability, owned LOC, and remaining platform limitations.
notes:
Priority P1: this is the smallest high-value feature in the roadmap because Orbit and Venus already carry the required authoritative URI. It is independent of later history, effects, semantic-region, workspace, observer, and graphics work.

External gate: implement only after an Orbit/Venus graduation go and the post-graduation ownership decision in Orbit orb-bi4.7, unless the user explicitly activates this Venus slice earlier.

Rejected alternatives: heuristic URL/path detection, an embedded browser, silent activation, client-side VT parsing, or a new general command framework.

Planning estimate: effort S; implementation risk MED (untrusted URI and native input/action policy); confidence HIGH.

title: Provide structured terminal accessibility
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C6 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Hardens VEN-C1 and VEN-C4 while consuming the exact Orbit presentation proof current at activation.
- Later ORB-C9 history and ORB-C10 semantic regions may enrich VEN-C6 but do not block a correct visible-viewport slice. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

Venus currently exposes the entire scene as one flattened AccessKit Terminal node. That announces content and failures but does not provide row structure, text ranges, selection, link navigation, or useful actions for screen-reader users.

## Evidence

- `src/accessibility.rs:31-40` creates one Terminal or Alert content node.
- `src/accessibility.rs:76-123` stores one flattened scene value.
- `src/scene.rs:203-214` concatenates the visible grid into accessible text.
- `src/accessibility.rs:169-173` proves only the flattened Terminal value and Alert.
- `docs/CRATES.md:12,65-76` assigns accessibility adaptation to AccessKit and requires it to derive from the accepted immutable scene.

## Scope

In scope:
- A bounded structured accessibility tree derived from the same accepted scene used for drawing.
- Stable visible row/text-run identity, text ranges and selection where AccessKit supports them, explicit link roles/actions, cursor/focus state, and failure/effect alerts.
- Keyboard and assistive-technology actions mapped through existing Venus interaction owners.
- Linux screen-reader dogfood and a macOS-credible tree/update design.

Out of scope:
- A second terminal document model, unbounded scrollback nodes, OCR/pixel inference, a custom accessibility framework, macOS support claims, or waiting for GPU presentation before answering an accessibility activation request.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Add user-approved VEN-C6 before code and record the exact consumed Orbit revision.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: AccessKit 0.24.1 tree, text, selection, action, focus, and live-region APIs; accesskit_winit 0.33.2 update/activation behavior; current Linux AT-SPI behavior; and one mature native terminal accessibility implementation at an exact revision. Classify later history/semantic sources as conditional.
3. Keep one Scene-derived accessibility projection. Use stable revision/row/run identities and window the tree to visible content plus only a deliberately bounded nearby range.
4. Route accessibility actions through existing Venus semantic input, selection, link, scroll, and copy owners. Never mutate a parallel content model.
5. Publish the latest accepted scene on activation even when rendering is occluded or recovering.
6. Add deterministic tree/action transition checks, then dogfood with at least one Linux screen reader. Compilation and snapshots alone do not prove usability.
7. When ORB-C9 or ORB-C10 later lands, extend the same tree with history windows and prompt/input/output landmarks instead of replacing it.

Dependency decision: reuse the accepted AccessKit stack. Any new accessibility crate, toolkit, or platform bridge requires a Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral scene-to-tree core with isolated platform adapters; actual macOS behavior remains unproved.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if required semantics are absent from the Orbit scene rather than inferring them.
- Stop if a proposed tree is unbounded or mirrors the entire terminal independently.
- Stop for user choice if AccessKit cannot express a required contract without another architecture-shaping dependency.
- Stop if deterministic checks pass but real assistive technology exposes a materially different interaction model; record the dogfood gap.
acceptance_criteria:
1. VEN-C6 is approved and indexed before implementation with the exact Orbit contracts and proof revision consumed.
2. The accessibility tree is derived solely from the accepted immutable Scene and cannot advance to unaccepted or stale presentation content.
3. Visible rows and text runs expose stable bounded structure, correct grapheme text, cursor/focus, link identity, selection/ranges where supported, and explicit status/effect alerts.
4. Accessibility activation receives a current tree even while the GPU surface is occluded, lost, or recovering.
5. Actions route through the same Venus interaction owners as pointer and keyboard behavior and never create terminal authority.
6. Tree size and update cost remain bounded under rapid output, resize, reconnect, large viewports, and status churn.
7. Strong deterministic checks cover tree transitions, IDs, Unicode, links, selection, actions, reconnect, occlusion, and failures.
8. Manual Linux screen-reader dogfood records navigation, reading order, focus, link activation, copy/selection, resize, and failure UX. Unsupported platform behavior remains explicit.
9. Locked canonical checks pass and closure records proof revision, dependency disposition, portability, LOC, dogfood environment, and limitations.
notes:
Priority P2: important product quality and a direct architectural advantage of structured presentation, but the existing flattened tree already provides a minimum accessible status/content baseline.

External gate: implement after an Orbit/Venus graduation go and orb-bi4.7 disposition unless the user explicitly activates it earlier. ORB-C9 and ORB-C10 are enhancements, not prerequisites for a bounded visible-screen improvement.

Rejected alternatives: one giant unstructured value as the final design, OCR, pixel scraping, exposing a full unbounded scrollback document, coupling accessibility updates to successful GPU presentation, or changing the terminal protocol solely to mirror AccessKit structures.

Planning estimate: effort M; implementation risk MED (assistive-technology behavior and update bounds); confidence MED until real Linux screen-reader dogfood validates the tree.

title: Prove Venus as a thin native client for Orbit
description: Prove the smallest useful native graphical materializer for one accepted Orbit session while preserving Orbit as the sole PTY and terminal authority. The initial experiment is one local Linux window, one active client, exact Orbit contract consumption, and no workspace feature expansion.
design:
ven-upt.1 completed the architecture, source, protocol, reference, and crate decisions. The user accepted that recommendation and activated ven-upt.2, which implemented the bounded first Linux slice. Venus consumes canonical ORBS v1, ORBF v1, and orbit-protocol 0.1.0 at accepted Orbit proof c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6 without a schema mirror or adapter.

The accepted ownership boundary remains unchanged: Orbit owns terminal authority and wire interpretation; Venus owns native presentation materialization and semantic interaction collection; Astra owns product orchestration and workspace policy. The client is one transient Linux window attached to one local Orbit session. Graphical code does not enter Orbit, and Venus owns no PTY, VT parser, second terminal emulator, or workspace policy.

VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 are proved at the exact source revisions indexed in docs/CONTRACTS.md. Subsequent bounded correctness and simplification passes advanced those proofs without expanding the product surface. Further product expansion, deferred Venus features, macOS implementation, packaging, distribution, and Astra implementation remain inactive until the user chooses them.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user explicitly accepts the Venus architecture and dependency recommendation and activates ven-upt.2 after the Orbit governance handoff.
2. Every implementation Bead follows the Execution baseline, Reference gate, Crate gate when triggered, contract-proof, portability, and closure rules in AGENTS.md.
3. VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 are either proved at exact accepted commits or retain explicit gaps.
4. Venus records every exact consumed Orbit proof revision and reports boundary gaps to Orbit rather than adding a second terminal or protocol owner.
5. The first client proves one useful Linux window, semantic interaction, reconnect, and bounded failure UX without expanding into workspace features.
6. No known P0 or P1 correctness risk remains unrecorded at the experiment decision boundary.
notes:
Both child Beads are closed: ven-upt.1 records the accepted dependency and architecture shape, and ven-upt.2 records the implemented first Linux slice. The final contract index proves VEN-C1 at fb1a4f152a52899cf74ecc47fa372d34333e7c4a, VEN-C2 at 7f87503173d1c8c17ca6997da6d2e04731e11b97, VEN-C3 at 13d7f8d59835a22b1e63e2d4cc087c081502668e, and VEN-C4 at fb1a4f152a52899cf74ecc47fa372d34333e7c4a, consuming accepted Orbit proof c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6. Canonical Rust checks and 30 tests were green at the final bounded review, which found no confirmed defect or worthwhile simplification.

No initial-slice Venus contract gap remains. Orbit retains partial ORB-C7 evidence, and its accepted c905bf proof is not yet published on origin/edge; docs/CONTRACTS.md records that external distribution gap. Wayland, macOS, packaging, distribution, hyperlinks, and richer accessibility remain explicitly unproved or deferred. Closing this epic activates no new feature, contract, dependency, platform, release, or Astra work.
close_reason: The accepted first Linux Venus slice is implemented and VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 are proved at their indexed exact revisions; the final bounded review found no remaining confirmed defect or worthwhile simplification, while all external and deferred gaps remain explicit.

title: Choose the minimum Venus backend and composition shape
description: Before any Cargo manifest or graphical implementation, choose the smallest backend, composition, text, and renderer ownership shape that can prove VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 against the accepted Orbit frame contract.
design: Pin ORB-C1 through ORB-C6, ORBF v1, ORBS v1, and canonical orbit-protocol 0.1.0 at accepted proof 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd; record partial ORB-C7 at the same revision. Venus will consume that package by exact Git revision without a schema mirror. The required exact-commit source gate is complete for Orbit, FrankenTUI, OpenTUI Rust, Ghostling, and libghostty-rs. The user selected winit 0.30.13, wgpu 30.0.0, glyphon 0.12.0 with its cosmic-text 0.19.0 re-export, AccessKit 0.24.1 and accesskit_winit 0.33.2, and pollster 1.0.1 after the measured crate gate and a second primary-source comparison. One pure revision-tagged scene reducer separates protocol, native host, renderer, and accessibility owners. The latest accepted scene feeds accessibility and deterministic evidence; successful presentation advances pointer hit geometry at a separate last-presented revision. Transport work wakes the winit loop through EventLoopProxy without selecting a general async application runtime. The first proof is deterministic full-scene reduction before native dogfood. This selection changes no product contract and authorizes no manifest or implementation until the user activates ven-upt.2.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline states that this is a research and dependency decision and changes no product contract by itself.
2. The decision records accepted Orbit proof 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd, consumed ORB-C1 through ORB-C6 plus partial ORB-C7, canonical protocol ownership, and exact-revision distribution before Venus code or manifest edits.
3. Venus does not handwrite or generate an independent mirror; protocol gaps return to Orbit.
4. The Reference gate records exact identities and evidence from Orbit, FrankenTUI, OpenTUI Rust, Ghostling, and libghostty-rs before code-shape selection.
5. Reference mechanisms and rejected TUI, terminal-owner, game-renderer, runtime, copied-source, and incompatible surrounding scope are explicit.
6. The Crate gate compares complete credible ownership shapes, including the smallest owned shape, with exact versions and measured evidence.
7. The decision recommends one native shape with owner boundaries, expected LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, first contract check, migration risk, and rollback condition.
8. No Cargo manifest, production decoder, renderer, compatibility layer, general UI framework, or Orbit distribution surface is added before explicit user approval.
notes: Decision complete at accepted Orbit proof 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd. The user selected the measured winit, wgpu, glyphon, and AccessKit shape. docs/CRATES.md records the ranked tradeoffs and owner seam; docs/REFERENCES.md records the exact primary-source mechanisms; append-only comments retain the full evidence. ven-upt.2 remains deferred and inactive pending explicit user activation. This Bead changes no VEN-C product contract and adds no Cargo, production, test, generated, packaging, or CI surface.

Reference gate — Jeffrey Emanuel rendering sources (2026-08-04): required source inspection completed for VEN-C1 through VEN-C4. Exact identities: Dicklesworthstone/frankentui at 479436597890a14e82676d0067e3917b2a9de8f5 and Dicklesworthstone/opentui_rust at a37bed1d2569fdd5d3bc33ec19c0678cd0cb1cd8. Inspected OpenTUI Rust OptimizedBuffer, ScissorStack, OpacityStack, draw-buffer composition, BufferDiff, Renderer present/resize/invalidate and layer paths, front/back hit grids, the application-owned loop, golden tests, and diff properties.

Independently useful mechanisms: keep platform event/time ownership separate from presentation; reduce accepted authoritative state through one deterministic composition path; retain a current candidate and last successfully presented state; publish interaction geometry only with the presentation revision it describes; treat resize, surface replacement, and geometry changes as explicit full-recomposition/full-redraw boundaries; keep a simple full-state fallback; use row-major deterministic ordering and reusable storage only where measured; make clipping a monotonic rectangle intersection and any approved nested opacity a clamped product; derive visual ordering and hit precedence in the same composition traversal; drive native and headless paths from the same semantic scene; prove state transitions and patch/damage invariants before optional pixel evidence. FrankenTUI ADR-009 is PROPOSED and no implemented first-party wgpu renderer was found, so its CPU instance buffer, bounded atlas, small constant draw-pass count, shared render/hit geometry, and patch-hash guidance are design hypotheses, not implementation proof. ADR-008 is also PROPOSED, although its small clock/event/presenter boundary exists and its focused tests pass.

Venus consequences: Orbit remains the only presentation and terminal-state author. Venus should materialize a complete accepted ORBF frame into one pure Venus-owned draw scene whose ordered visual inputs and hyperlink or other contract-approved hit metadata share the same Orbit revision. The native host owns window, input, surface lifecycle, and failure UX; the renderer consumes the scene and does not parse transport or terminal state. Candidate and presented scene/hit state must advance together only after successful present. Because current Orbit input is complete frames, Venus should first rebuild the scene deterministically and full redraw; local damage may be derived later from consecutive accepted scenes after measurement and must not become a second wire protocol. Initial Venus has no approved general layer, popup, widget, or alpha-composition feature, so OpenTUI stack mechanics are conditional patterns rather than new scope.

Rejected surrounding scope: all ANSI and raw-terminal presentation, VT or input parsing, terminal capability policy, TUI widgets/runtime, generic widget registries, per-project grapheme/link pools, web bridge, DOM/canvas path, threaded renderer, and direct source reuse. Also rejected for the first slice are FrankenTUI dirty-row plus dirty-span plus bitmap plus tile plus certificate machinery, adaptive resize allocation policy, Bayesian or scheduler machinery, patch transport, and an eager custom glyph atlas. OpenTUI Renderer itself is not a Venus boundary because it bundles terminal lifecycle, output, buffers, layers, pools, hit state, timing, and statistics. Its cell grid is evidence for composition semantics, not the final GPU/text representation.

First meaningful Venus check: a bounded canonical ORBF corpus reduces repeated runs to byte-for-byte identical ordered draw-scene snapshots and revision-tagged hit metadata; properties cover viewport bounds, wide head/spacer consistency, cursor and hyperlink alignment, deterministic order, stale/out-of-order revision rejection, resize invalidation, and complete fallback recomposition. Headless evidence proves state/composition only; font quality, IME, accessibility, GPU/window lifecycle, and visual quality remain manual/native proof surfaces.

Verification evidence: cargo test -p ftui-backend passed 23 tests; cargo test -p ftui-render --test headless_integration passed 5 tests; focused OpenTUI tests test_scissor_stack, test_opacity_multiply, test_present_swaps_buffers, test_renderer_hit_test_after_present, and test_merge_layers_composites_hit_grids_by_layer_id each passed. The wgpu renderer owns device, surface, simple rectangle/decorations pipeline, and present outcome. Glyphon owns shaping, fallback, raster cache/atlas, clipping, and text draw preparation. Candidate and last-successfully-presented scene, hit, and accessibility state advance together only after successful present. Start with deterministic full scene rebuild and full redraw; derive local damage only after measurement and never as wire state.

Candidate B saves only four measured package entries but adds roughly 700-1,200 specialized atlas/shader/cache LOC and security/maintenance risk. Candidate C is about 300-600 renderer LOC but carries CPU scaling and pixel-buffer costs. D and the full frameworks own far more layout/runtime policy than one custom surface needs. Skia adds a large C++ binary/build/Nix surface; femtovg makes OpenGL and another text stack architecture-shaping; Sugarloaf is active terminal-product machinery with backend churn; Ghostling paths import terminal authority or demo-grade rendering; a fully owned stack duplicates windowing, GPU, shaping, fallback, accessibility, and macOS work.

Headless evidence never claims visual quality.

Rollback condition: if the bounded corpus plus native dogfood shows that glyphon cannot preserve exact grapheme fallback, cell alignment, clipping, color glyphs, or sustained redraw latency within the accepted threshold, retain protocol, scene, winit, wgpu, and AccessKit owners and reopen a narrow text-renderer gate comparing an owned cosmic-text atlas with the current Sugarloaf mechanism. title: Render one accepted Orbit session in a minimum Linux window
description: Implement the smallest Venus slice: one Linux window consumes canonical structured frames from an already-running Orbit session, renders their accepted rich state, sends semantic input and resize, remains transient across client exit, and explains bounded attachment or server failure.
design:
Begin only after the user activates Venus, accepts the backend and composition decision, and accepts one exact-revision canonical Orbit protocol-consumption shape. Pin the exact accepted Orbit commit and ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states. Decode accepted ORBF v1 complete frames into one persistent Venus PresentationState before producing draw inputs; reconnect and resync replace that state coherently. This keeps a later user-approved patch protocol compatible with the same reducer model without implementing patches now.

Before manual window dogfood, use a bounded canonical frame corpus or the smallest protocol-faithful source to prove deterministic decode and frame-to-draw inputs without a live PTY, handwritten mirror schema, raw VT parser, or second terminal authority. Keep Linux window and GPU mechanics inside Venus and report any protocol gap to Orbit through separate owner commits and compatibility sequencing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user activates Venus, Orbit orb-9o6 is closed, and the accepted protocol-consumption plus backend and composition decisions are recorded before implementation.
2. The Execution baseline records the exact Orbit proof commit, consumed ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states, affected VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 contracts, intended surfaces, and pre-existing worktree state.
3. The pre-code Reference gate and accepted Crate gate satisfy AGENTS.md; manifest changes match the user-approved protocol and dependency shapes exactly.
4. A focused nonvisual check consumes canonical Orbit ORBF v1 frames, applies complete frames and ordered revisions to one bounded persistent PresentationState, and deterministically produces draw inputs for styled Unicode and graphemes, cursor, alternate screen, reconnect, and failure cases.
5. One Linux window attaches to an already-running Orbit session, renders coherent current state, and sends semantic keyboard input and resize through Orbit.
6. Closing or crashing Venus leaves Orbit and the PTY alive; reopening receives and applies coherent current state.
7. Attach rejection, incompatible or invalid frames, revision failures, and Orbit loss produce clear bounded failures rather than hangs or invented state.
8. Venus owns no PTY, terminal emulator, terminal-query response, raw VT parser, mirrored protocol schema, terminal history content, workspace topology, or Astra policy.
9. Closure records deterministic checks, manual visual dogfood, owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, exact Orbit compatibility, proof revisions, and remaining gaps.
10. Patches, history pages, ordered terminal effects, richer resources, tabs, panes, sidebars, popups, settings, visual effects, configuration, plugins, remote or web access, macOS implementation, packaging, and distribution remain excluded.
